cards.text: Later, Belshazzar is king of Babylon. He throws a great feast for a thousand of his nobles, and he drinks wine with them. A THOUSAND guests, friend, and I can't fit a dozen cookies on one tray without one sliding off.
Under the influence of the wine, Belshazzar gives an order. He wants the gold and silver vessels brought in, the ones his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken.

cards.question: Belshazzar wants the gold and silver vessels his father Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple in ___.
Belshazzar orders the vessels from the temple brought into his feast. Why?

answers.text: So they can drink from them
So they can be sent back
So they can be melted down

cards.text: So in come the gold vessels taken from the temple, the house of God in Jerusalem. The king drinks from them with his nobles, his wives and his concubines.

cards.question: While Belshazzar and his guests drink wine from the vessels of God's house, they praise their gods made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood and stone.

cards.text: At that moment, the fingers of a human hand appear and write on the plaster of the wall, near the lampstand in the royal palace. And the king is watching the hand as it writes.

cards.question: Belshazzar watches the hand writing on his palace wall. What happens to him?

answers.text: His face grows pale and his knees knock together
He laughs and lifts his cup toward the hand
He jumps up and shouts for his palace guards

cards.text: His thoughts alarm him so much that his hips give way. Knees knocking in front of a thousand nobles, friend, and I'd be knocking too, and I don't even HAVE knees.

cards.question: Shaking, Belshazzar calls out for help with the writing on the wall. Who does he call for?

cards.text: He offers whoever reads the writing and explains it purple clothes, a gold chain around the neck and the spot of third highest ruler in the kingdom. Friend, that's a PROMOTION for reading one wall.

cards.question: All of Belshazzar's wise men come in to look at the writing on the wall. What can they do with it?

answers.text: Neither read it nor interpret it
Read it but not interpret it
Interpret it but not read it

cards.question: Once Belshazzar's wise men come up empty on the writing, the king calms down.

cards.text: His face grows even more pale, and his nobles are bewildered. Friend, that's like calling the repair guy and watching HIM scratch his head.
Then the queen hears the outcry and walks into the banquet hall. She says, “O king, may you live forever!” and tells him, “Do not let your thoughts terrify you, or your face grow pale.”

cards.question: The queen tells Belshazzar there's a man in his kingdom with the spirit of the holy gods in him. Which king made that man chief of the magicians?

cards.text: The man's name is Daniel, the one Nebuchadnezzar named Belteshazzar. The queen says he has an extraordinary spirit, and he can interpret dreams, explain riddles and solve difficult problems.

cards.question: The queen tells Belshazzar to summon Daniel. What does she say Daniel will do?

answers.text: Copy the writing onto a scroll

cards.text: Daniel is brought in, and Belshazzar asks him, “Are you Daniel, one of the exiles my father the king brought from Judah?”

Belshazzar's heard Daniel has extraordinary wisdom, and his own wise men came up empty, so he makes Daniel the same offer: purple clothes, a gold chain and third highest ruler in the kingdom. Same prize nobody could reach the first time, friend, like a cookie box on the top shelf.

cards.question: Daniel tells Belshazzar he will gladly accept the purple clothes and the gold chain.
Daniel turns down Belshazzar's gifts. What does he say he will still do?

answers.text: Read the inscription and interpret it
Pray for the king through the night
Ask his God to erase the writing

cards.text: Before Daniel reads a word, he tells the king about his father: the Most High God gave Nebuchadnezzar sovereignty and greatness, glory and honor. The king asked for a reading, friend, and he's getting a family history.

Because of that greatness, people of every nation and language trembled in fear before Nebuchadnezzar. He killed whom he wished and kept alive whom he wished, and he exalted and humbled whom he wished.

cards.question: Daniel says Nebuchadnezzar's heart became arrogant and his spirit was hardened with pride. What happened to Nebuchadnezzar then?

answers.text: He was deposed from his throne
He built a new royal palace

cards.text: He was driven away from mankind, and his mind was like that of a beast. He ate grass like an ox until he acknowledged that the Most High God rules over the kingdom of mankind, setting over it whom He wishes.

cards.question: Daniel says Belshazzar never knew what happened to his father Nebuchadnezzar.

cards.text: Daniel says Belshazzar has not humbled his heart but exalted himself against the Lord of heaven, praising gods of silver and gold, bronze and iron, wood and stone, “which cannot see or hear or understand.” Friend, that's like thanking my rolling pin for a great batch, and it can't hear me either.

cards.question: Belshazzar praised gods that cannot see or hear, and Daniel says he failed to glorify the true God. How does Daniel describe that God?

answers.text: He holds the king's very breath in His hand
He leaves the king to rule his own ways
He shares His glory with the gods of gold

cards.question: Daniel says the hand that wrote on the wall was sent by the gods Belshazzar praised.

cards.text: Then Daniel reads the inscription: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN. Four words, friend, and I've written longer notes asking somebody to preheat the oven.

cards.question: MENE is the first word on Belshazzar's wall. What does Daniel say it means?

answers.text: God has numbered the days of his reign
God has forgiven the pride of the king
God will add more years to his reign

cards.question: Daniel says TEKEL means Belshazzar has been weighed on the scales and found ___.
Daniel says PERES means Belshazzar's kingdom has been divided and given over to the ___ and Persians.
After hearing all that, Belshazzar still has Daniel clothed in purple and proclaimed third highest ruler in the kingdom.

cards.text: That very night, Belshazzar king of the Chaldeans is slain.

cards.question: Belshazzar is slain that very night. Who receives his kingdom?

cards.text: Darius the Mede receives the kingdom at the age of sixty-two.
